title: Phonon dynamics in Chromium under pressure: absence of phonon criticality at the approach of the quantum critical point
authors: P. Rodière, J. E. Lorenzo, Q. N. Meier, L. Paolasini, A. Bosak
abstract: Fermi surface nesting is key to understanding the origin of the itinerant antiferromagnetic spin density wave in Chromium. At very low temperature, this density wave is destroyed above the critical pressure $P_c\approx$10~GPa, defining a quantum critical point. Strong electron-phonon coupling induces a small phonon softening close to the $H-$point of the Brillouin zone as well as close to the $H$-point. These phonon anomalies are known as Kohn anomalies. They remain unchanged down to 50K and are known to be present in both the paramagnetic and the antiferromagnetic phases. This paper presents inelastic X-ray scattering experiments on the phonon dispersion curves under pressure, up to $P=$15.6~GPa far above the critical pressure $P_c$. The softening of the well-known phonon anomalies is still present which leads to conclude that they do not play a major role at the antiferromagnetic ordering. Based on ab-initio calculation, the robustness of the Fermi surface nesting under pressure, explain the presence of these Kohn anomalies above the critical pressure.
summary: This work uses inelastic X-ray scattering and DFT calculations to examine phonon behavior in Chromium as pressure approaches its antiferromagnetic quantum critical point. The key finding is that the observed phonon anomalies are robustly linked to Fermi surface nesting, suggesting that the SDW ordering mechanism is electronic rather than being driven by lattice instabilities (phonons) near $P_c$. This refines our understanding of itinerant magnetism at QCPs.
main_problem: The study investigates phonon dynamics in Chromium under high pressure, specifically addressing whether lattice anomalies (Kohn anomalies) play a major role near the quantum critical point (QCP).
main_result: The persistence of Kohn anomalies and the robustness of Fermi surface nesting suggest that these anomalies do not drive the antiferromagnetic ordering at high pressures.
method: The research combines inelastic X-ray scattering experiments with ab-initio Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations using DFPT for phonon dispersion analysis.
model_or_system: The system is Chromium (Cr), an archetype material exhibiting itinerant antiferromagnetic spin density wave (SDW) ordering, studied under varying pressures up to 15.6 GPa.
key_observables: Phonon dispersion curves, Kohn anomalies (phonon softening), and the evolution of the Fermi surface nesting function ($\chi''(\mathbf{q})$).
important_parameters: Critical pressure ($P_c \approx 10$ GPa), high pressures up to $15.6$ GPa, and low temperatures.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the SDW formation is the primary order parameter, and Kohn anomalies are primarily driven by electronic susceptibility rather than direct lattice instability near the QCP.
figures_summary: Figures show phonon spectra/dispersion curves at ambient and high pressure along $\Gamma	ext{H}$ and $\Gamma	ext{N}$, illustrating the persistence of softening features despite crossing $P_c$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the background on SDW formation in Cr, presents experimental measurements of phonon anomalies under pressure, compares these findings with DFT calculations showing robust nesting, and concludes that electronic susceptibility dictates the QCP behavior.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the interplay between lattice dynamics (phonons) and electronic instabilities (SDW/CDW) near a quantum critical point involves many-body physics relevant to strongly correlated systems.
